question.text: Will the FDA approve BridgeBio's BBP-418 (ribitol) for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 by November 27, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) grants approval of BridgeBio Pharma's New Drug Application for BBP-418 (ribitol) for the treatment of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9) on or before November 27, 2026. Approval counts whether it is granted under the traditional or the accelerated approval pathway, and regardless of the exact wording or breadth of the approved indication. The primary resolution source is BridgeBio's press release feed at https://investor.bridgebio.com/news/default.aspx; the FDA action date, not the date of public announcement, determines whether approval occurred on or before November 27, 2026. If no FDA approval of the BBP-418 NDA for LGMD2I/R9 has been granted on or before November 27, 2026 — including if the FDA issues a complete response letter or extends the PDUFA target action date without deciding — this question resolves NO. If the BridgeBio feed is unavailable, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: If approval is granted on or before November 27, 2026 but only becomes publicly reported afterwards (for example over the weekend of November 28–29, 2026), the question still resolves YES. The question does not remain open for an FDA decision taken after November 27, 2026.

research:
Nothing settles this yet. As of 2026-11-16, the FDA has not approved BBP-418, issued a complete response letter, or extended the review. The November 27, 2026 target date still stands, and Kalshi prices approval in 2026 at about 90%.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: The news page on BridgeBio's site loads its list with a script. I read the underlying data feed directly. The newest release is dated 2026-11-11 (acoramidis data at an amyloidosis meeting). Before that come 11-09 (investor conferences), 11-06 (inducement grants), 11-03 (acoramidis data at the American Heart Association meeting) and 10-29 (Q3 results). None of them reports an FDA action on BBP-418. [feed](https://investor.bridgebio.com/feed/PressRelease.svc/GetPressReleaseList?LanguageId=1&bodyType=0&pressReleaseDateFilter=3&categoryId=1cb807d2-208f-4bc3-9133-6a9ad45ac3b0&pageSize=10&pageNumber=0&tagList=&includeTags=true&year=2026&excludeSelection=1), [newsroom](https://investor.bridgebio.com/news/default.aspx)
- 2026-11-16: Drugs.com still lists BBP-418 as not FDA approved. [Drugs.com](https://www.drugs.com/history/bbp-418.html)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that settles the question. I found no approval, no complete response letter and no announced extension of the target date.
- 2026-05-27: The FDA accepted the application with Priority Review and set a target action date of November 27, 2026. No advisory committee meeting is planned. [BridgeBio PR](https://investor.bridgebio.com/news/news-details/2026/BridgeBio-Announces-FDA-Acceptance-and-Priority-Review-of-NDA-for-BBP-418-for-LGMD2IR9/default.aspx), [BioSpace](https://www.biospace.com/fda/fda-accepts-bridgebios-application-for-potential-first-limb-girdle-muscular-dystrophy-drug)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: At the Jefferies Healthcare Conference in London, CEO Neil Kumar pointed to the November 27 decision date and called the trial results a "remarkable data set" (improvements in walking, breathing and other measures). This comes from the news-API summary; I did not check the audio. [BiotechTV podcast](https://anchor.fm/s/101538d68/podcast/play/129538522/https%3A%2F%2Fd3ctxlq1ktw2nl.cloudfront.net%2Fstaging%2F2026-10-16%2F436859262-44100-2-f30dab8b3aadd8.mp3)
- 2026-11-14: Morgan Stanley raised its price target on BridgeBio. [dailypolitical](https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/11/14/bridgebio-pharma-nasdaqbbio-stock-price-target-raised-at-morgan-stanley.html)
- 2026-11-16: The same week brings other FDA decisions, including Capricor's deramiocel for Duchenne and Savara's molgramostim (both due Nov 22). Summit Therapeutics' lung-cancer drug was recently rejected, a reminder that rejections do happen. [Stocktwits](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/three-fda-decisions-summit-rejection-capricor-savara-alzheimer-data-biotech-watchlist/cNb7eF1R9XR)
- 2026-10-29: In the Q3 release, the CEO said the company was "weeks away from the potential approval" and that launch preparation was "well advanced." [Q3 PR](https://investor.bridgebio.com/news/news-details/2026/BridgeBio-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-and-Corporate-Updates/default.aspx)
  - BridgeBio has identified more than 500 U.S. patients, and about 70% are treated at MDA Care Centers.
  - Sales staff have reached more than 70% of MDA centers, with a goal of at least 90% by the target date.
  - It still says no advisory committee is planned.
  - New cardiac data from the trial: troponin returned to normal in 100% of treated patients vs 40% on placebo (p=0.0248), and heart pumping function (LVEF) was stable or improved in 54% vs 25% (p=0.0262).
  - The European filing will wait for the 36-month final analysis (topline late 2027 or early 2028).
- 2026-03-30: BridgeBio submitted the NDA, based on the 12-month interim analysis of the Phase 3 FORTIFY trial. [MD News](https://musculardystrophynews.com/news/bridgebio-asks-fda-approve-potential-1st-treatment-lgmd2i/)

## 4. Base rates
- Applications with Priority Review and Orphan, Fast Track and Rare Pediatric Disease designations usually get first-cycle approval at fairly high rates. I could not find an exact recent figure for this group.
- A review can be extended by three months if the company submits a major amendment late in the review. Your background notes that three of the 18 Q4 2026 decisions had already been extended. A late extension would make this question resolve NO.
- The FDA can approve a drug before its target date, and Friday decisions sometimes come out after markets close. A November 27 action reported over the weekend would still count as YES.
- Specific risk here: the filing relies on interim data and a biomarker (glycosylated alpha-dystroglycan) rather than a completed Phase 3, although BridgeBio says the FDA steered it toward traditional approval.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-11-16 18:37 UTC: Kalshi's "FDA decision: BBP-418 … this year" market has Yes (full or accelerated approval) at **0.90**. Its window is calendar 2026, wider than this question's November 27 cutoff, so it slightly overstates the chance of approval by the 27th.
- Jefferies analysts have reportedly said they have "90%+ confidence" in full approval. This came from a search summary and I did not see the primary note.
- Your background cites BiopharmaWatch at about 78%; I did not verify it.
- I found no Polymarket, Manifold or Metaculus market on this drug.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- November 2026 investor conferences (Jefferies London, among others): management comments could hint at label talks or an extension.
- 2026-11-22: FDA decisions on Capricor and Savara could show how the FDA is treating rare-disease applications right now.
- 2026-11-26: Thanksgiving, the day before the target date. The 27th is a short, quiet day for the FDA, which raises the chance the action comes earlier or the news slips into the weekend.
- 2026-11-27 (Friday): target action date. A three-month extension would most likely be announced before then.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The outcome will be known in about 11 days, with the PDUFA target on Friday, November 27, 2026, the day after Thanksgiving. For Yes, the FDA has to approve the BBP-418 NDA for LGMD2I/R9, under traditional or accelerated approval, on or before November 27. An approval dated the 27th but reported over the weekend still counts.

(b) If nothing changes, no decision has been announced. The default path for a priority-review NDA with no advisory committee and no reported FDA concerns is an on-time action. The open question is whether that action is an approval or a CRL, plus a small chance of a late extension.

(c) Base rate: first-cycle approval for novel NDAs with Priority Review, Orphan and Fast Track status, no AdCom and positive pivotal data runs at roughly 85-90%. The 2025-2026 rare-disease CRL wave (at least 23 CRLs) pulls this down somewhat, so about 82-85%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - FORTIFY's interim analysis met all primary and secondary endpoints, and supportive cardiac data was released on 2026-10-29.
  - The FDA recommended orienting the NDA toward traditional approval.
  - No AdCom was planned (May 27, reiterated Oct 29), and no concerns have been disclosed.
  - The CEO's "weeks away" comment came on Oct 29, and the PDUFA date was reaffirmed at Jefferies on 2026-11-16.
  - Jefferies puts the odds above 90% (Nov 2).
  - Kalshi prices 2026 approval at 0.90 (Nov 16).
  - No extension has been announced with 11 days left.
- **For No:**
  - The filing rests on an interim analysis and a biomarker, from a single trial with primary completion in July 2027.
  - The FDA's current stance on rare-disease applications is stricter, with several 2026 CRLs (Atara, REGENXBIO, Disc).
  - Late extensions happen: 3 of 18 Q4 decisions were pushed back.
  - The Thanksgiving timing slightly raises the risk of a missed date.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** The FDA issues a CRL around Nov 25-27 asking for the completed 36-month FORTIFY data to confirm functional benefit. Alternatively, a late major-amendment request triggers a three-month extension.
- **Yes:** The FDA approves on Nov 24-26 with a label requiring genetic confirmation, and BridgeBio announces it immediately.

(f) I anchor on Kalshi's 0.90. That market's window is all of 2026, so I subtract about 2-3 points for a December approval after a short slip or an extension, which would still resolve this question NO. I take another point or so off for interim-data risk in the current FDA climate. That gives about 86%, consistent with a base rate adjusted upward for strong data and the absence of any negative signals.

Probability: 86%

**(a) Time left and what Yes requires:** About 11 days remain. The PDUFA target action date is Friday, November 27, 2026. For Yes, the FDA must approve the BBP-418 NDA, by either the traditional or accelerated pathway, with an action date on or before November 27. The approval can be announced afterwards, for example over the weekend.

**(b) Status quo:** The review is ongoing, with no CRL and no extension announced. The usual outcome for an application in this position is approval on or near the PDUFA date. If the FDA simply did nothing, the question would resolve No, but that is not the realistic default here.

**(c) Base rate:** Novel NDAs with priority review, no advisory committee, positive Phase 3 data and orphan or rare pediatric designations are approved on the first cycle roughly 85-90% of the time. The 2025-2026 FDA has issued more rare-disease CRLs, at least 23 since 2025, and has occasionally missed PDUFA dates. That pulls the base rate down to about 80-85%.

**(d) Strongest evidence:**

For Yes:
- The FDA itself recommended orienting the NDA toward traditional approval.
- All prespecified primary and secondary endpoints were met at the interim analysis.
- Supportive cardiac data were released on 2026-10-29.
- No advisory committee is planned, reiterated on 2026-10-29.
- No extension had been announced as of 2026-11-16. Extensions usually come weeks before the action date.
- The CEO remained confident at Jefferies London on 2026-11-16.
- Jefferies puts approval odds above 90% (2026-11-02).
- Kalshi prices approval in 2026 at 0.90 (2026-11-16).

For No:
- The filing rests on an interim analysis of a single trial, with completion not until July 2027, and partly on a biomarker.
- The current FDA appears to be tougher on "one trial plus confirmatory evidence" applications, with rare-disease CRLs in 2026 (Atara, REGENXBIO, Disc).
- 3 of the 18 Q4 2026 decisions had already been extended.
- The Thanksgiving-adjacent date adds a small risk of a missed date.

**(e) Scenarios:**
